title: Silverline Onramp: credits, time-to-first-token, and privacy pathway
summary: Introductory discovery call focused on Silverline's PLG onramp. Main topics: free credits and quickstart timeline, choosing hosted vs dedicated vs private for media personalization workloads, security/compliance requirements (SOC2, VPC, KMS), success criteria (latency < 200ms for snippet gen, cost targets), and pilot next steps including a small-scale benchmark. Redwood to send pricing, security pack, and pilot runbook.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
security: SOC 2, VPC, KMS, data retention
transcript:
Meeting header - 2026-02-14 16:00 PST | Duration: ~42m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Jorge Ramos (Silverline, Head of Product), Mei Lin (Silverline, Eng Manager), Daniel K. (Silverline, CTO)
---
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy Valentines day, quick intro - I'm Maya, AE on the team, with Ravi who's our systems engineer.
[00:12] Jorge Ramos: Hi all, Jorge here. Thanks for fitting us in, we're trying to figure out timeline to ship a personalization snippet into our app and want to see how fast we can get to first token with Redwood.
[00:22] Ravi Patel: Great, yeah, we'll walk through the quickstart flow, credits, and then security which I know is key for media. Quick note, I might use some shorthand like DPC for ded- capacity, sorry old habit.
[00:35] Mei Lin: No problem. Also high-level constraint: we need to keep customer PII off third-party hosts unless encrypted and auditable.
[00:44] Daniel K.: And cost target - we run millions of short generation requests a day; we need to understand per-token economics and potential savings with batching/caching.
[00:53] Maya Chen: Perfect, that's exactly what we'll cover. First, quickstart: we offer self-serve sign-up, you get starter credits for PLG trials. Typical time-to-first-token for a developer is under 20 minutes if they're using the hosted API and have a simple prompt set. We can also give credits that map to roughly X tokens for experimenting.
[01:12] Jorge Ramos: When you say "starter credits," what's typical? Are those enough to do a small throughput eval?
[01:20] Maya Chen: Usually we provide a $2,000 pilot credit for enterprise trials — that's configurable — enough for tens of millions short-token calls depending on model. For self-serve PLG it's smaller (a few hundred dollars) but you can request an uplift for an evaluation.
[01:32] Mei Lin: Okay. For our purposes we want to run a sample of 100k requests across three prompt variants and measure latency and cost. Can that fit in the enterprise pilot?
[01:43] Ravi Patel: Yep, that fits. On hosted, latency to first token will depend on model and region; for the small models we vet you can expect p50 ~ 120-180ms for short prompts, p95 higher. If you need strict p99 SLAs, that's where dedicated capacity comes in.
[01:58] Daniel K.: Dedicated — is that physical reserved GPUs or a tenant on your infra? How isolated is it?
[02:06] Ravi Patel: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools — predictable throughput and isolation. Data plane is still managed by Redwood but isolated pools and no noisy neighbor. For full control, Private deployments run a customer-managed control plane in your VPC or on-prem. Private also supports HSM/KMS integrations for key custody.
[02:22] Jorge Ramos: Cool. We're interested in private eventually because of our publisher contracts, but for quick iteration we'd rather start hosted. Is it straightforward to migrate from hosted to dedicated/private later?
[02:34] Maya Chen: Yes, that's a core design — same API and config. You can pin model versions and rollout rules; we support canary and A/B during migration so switching endpoints is minimal work. We usually recommend starting hosted for time-to-first-token and then lift-and-shift to dedicated when throughput or compliance demands it.
[02:50] Mei Lin: About data: if we point requests to hosted, what's Redwood's retention policy? Can you redact or disable logging for specific routes?
[02:59] Ravi Patel: We retain logs per customer policy. For enterprise pilots we typically set short retention, and you can request no retention for certain endpoints. We also offer encryption-at-rest with customer-managed keys, and audit logs sent to your SIEM. We'll attach the SOC2 / security pack after the call.
[03:14] Maya Chen: (note) we'll share a link to security pack and the private deployment checklist.
[03:20] Jorge Ramos: Great. On model side: are you providing model variants? We need models tuned for content brevity and brand voice.
[03:30] Ravi Patel: We curate open models and provide performance profiles — also Redwood Optimize suggests quantization and batching profiles for cost/perf. For brand voice, you can fine-tune or use prompt-engineered templates. We also support function calling-style structured outputs for downstream rendering.
[03:45] Daniel K.: Any support for rate limiting per token or per user? We have per-request rate caps for downstream billing.
[03:52] Maya Chen: Yes, token-level quotas and per-route caps; you can throttle by API key and by route. We'll also surface token-level cost traces in the console.
[04:01] Mei Lin: For the benchmark, we want to push 200 QPS over a 10 minute window to mimic peak. Will hosted handle bursting?
[04:10] Ravi Patel: Hosted can burst but consistent 200 QPS for small models is usually fine. If you need guaranteed throughput you reserve Dedicated capacity. For benchmarks, we recommend running first on hosted with your real prompt set and we'll help interpret KV-cache and batching behavior — that often reduces token cost significantly.
[04:30] Jorge Ramos: Are there any gotchas for short snippet gen? We need <200ms median across US users.
[04:36] Ravi Patel: Short prompts are sensitive to cold starts — prefix caching helps. Also model choice and sequence length matter. We'll propose a config that keeps prefix caching enabled, and if you see p50 <200ms but p95 spikes, we can recommend autoscale and fallback model variants to trade slight quality for latency.
[04:55] Maya Chen: Quick note on pricing: hosted per-token; Dedicated is committed monthly and better for unit economics at scale. We can share an estimate spreadsheet based on your expected QPS and payload sizes.
[05:05] MeI Lin: (audio glitch) sorry, Mei.
[05:08] Mei Lin: No worries. Can Redwood support SSO/SAML and RBAC for teams?
[05:14] Maya Chen: Yes, SSO with SAML/SCIM provisioning and fine-grained RBAC is standard for enterprise. We'll include guides in the security pack.
[05:22] Jorge Ramos: Timeline — if we wanted to do a pilot next week, what's realistic?
[05:27] Maya Chen: For hosted pilot, day 0: create account and we hand out pilot credits; day 1: devs can hit endpoints and run tests. We can schedule a benchmark session with Ravi where we watch live telemetry. End-to-end in one week is realistic. For Dedicated, procurement lead time is longer (2-4 weeks) due to capacity reservation and contract.
[05:45] Ravi Patel: For the benchmark session, I'll provide a runbook: test prompt set, QPS pattern, latency metrics to capture. We'll also provide a small test harness script.
[05:57] Daniel K.: For the pilot contract and IP, do you have standard terms for data ownership and deletion?
[06:03] Maya Chen: Yes, standard enterprise addendum covers data ownership, deletion requests, and a 30-day data purge upon contract end. For Private deployments on-prem or in VPC you keep full ownership.
[06:14] Jorge Ramos: About competition — we kicked the tires on Anthropic and Vertex but reliability and predictable cost were pain points. How do you compare on observability?
[06:25] Ravi Patel: Our Console exposes per-route, per-model token & latency breakdowns, tracing hooks, and a quality/regression alert tied to prompt evals. That visibility plus Optimize suggestions for batching is our differentiator.
[06:39] Mei Lin: Ok seems reasonable. Next steps?
[06:42] Maya Chen: I'll recap: 1) We'll send pricing and an estimated cost spreadsheet based on your 100k request plan; 2) Send security pack and SOC2 docs + private deployment checklist; 3) Ravi will share benchmark runbook and a small test harness; 4) Schedule a live benchmark/telemetry session next Wednesday if that works.
[06:58] Jorge Ramos: Next Wed works. Also we'll share a small prompt set and sample user traffic profile.
[07:04] Daniel K.: Action on contract team-if pilot looks good, we expect to start procurement for Dedicated in ~60 days.
[07:10] Maya Chen: Sounds good.
[07:15] (brief cross talk)
[07:20] Ravi Patel: I'll also note some potential optimizations when you run the benchmark — kv cache, prefix reuse, and a likely 20-30% cost reduction from batching for your particular payload sizes.
[07:33] Mei Lin: Nice. Any recommended models to start with for brevity and speed?
[07:39] Ravi Patel: We often recommend the trimmed open LLMs we list in the quickstart — model A for fastest, B for slightly higher quality. We'll include performance profiles in the email.
[07:49] Jorge Ramos: Can you do a simple cost projection: if we run 100k short calls with avg 30 tokens output, what's the rough hosted spend?
[07:58] Maya Chen: We'll compute that precisely in the spreadsheet but very rough: if a token costs $0.000004, 100k * 30 tokens = 3M tokens which is about $12 at that rate; but model variability matters. We'll send detailed numbers.
[08:15] Daniel K.: That pricing seems low — I think you mean $0.00004?
[08:20] Maya Chen: Sorry yeah typo — we'll send correct numbers.
[08:24] (laughter)
[08:29] Maya Chen: Okay, I'll follow up with the spreadsheet and security docs. Ravi will attach the runbook and test harness repo. Jorge/Mei to share prompt set and target QPS.
[08:40] Jorge Ramos: Great, thanks all.
[08:43] Mei Lin: Thanks.
[08:45] Daniel K.: Thanks, bye.
[08:47] Maya Chen: Bye!
---
